Subject: MSA & Order Form — governing law, seat, and injunctive relief proposals

Hi Ian / Harper Contracts team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier this week. As promised I’m attaching an updated MSA redline and the clean Order Form for you to circulate internally (MSA_Redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_Clean.pdf). Two narrow areas we want to resolve so we can get legal sign-off and move to PO/DocuSign: governing law/venue and interim injunctive relief.

Summary of our position (short):
- Governing law: Delaware (commercial contract law familiarity; consistent with other enterprise customers).
- Dispute resolution: binding arbitration for covered claims (AAA/ICDR rules) with seat in San Francisco (neutral, enforceable).
- Interim relief: we can accept a narrow carveout allowing customer to seek provisional/injunctive relief in the customer’s local court (Northern District of California or state courts) only for preservation of evidence, protection of trade secrets/IP, or urgent data protection issues. Any remedy beyond preservation should remain for the arbitrator.

Rationale: arbitration + Delaware law keeps the ongoing dispute path predictable; the limited carveout preserves Harper’s ability to protect customer data and IP quickly. The redline includes proposed language that limits scope and imposes expedited meet-and-confer steps before resort to court to minimize forum-shopping.

Can you confirm whether this is workable for Harper, or send your counter-language? If we can land this compromise we’ll get final sign-off from Legal and Treasury and share a DocuSign envelope by COB Friday.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — governing law, seat, and injunctive relief proposals

Dylan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redline. Harper’s general counsel reviewed and asked that we push back on two points: governing law and the mechanism for emergency relief. Our counterproposal is below and we’ve attached an annotated redline (Harper_MSARedline_annotated.docx).

Harper position (high level):
- Governing law: California (Harper is headquartered in SF and prefers local commercial law).
- Emergency relief: customer must be able to file for provisional/injunctive relief in California state or federal court (Northern District of CA) where Harper is based. We’re willing to limit injunctive relief to the categories you mentioned (IP, data protection, preservation), but we cannot accept language that requires arbitration as the exclusive first step for emergency measures.
- Arbitration seat: we’re fine with arbitration for merits, but ask that the arbitration seat default to a neutral East/West location (we proposed San Jose or San Francisco).

Suggested compromise language (summary):
- Choice of law: Governing Law: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to conflicts of law principles."
- Emergency relief: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in the state and federal courts located in the Northern District of California for the limited purpose of preserving rights related to trade secrets, IP, or urgent data security matters; such relief shall not constitute a waiver of the parties' agreement to arbitrate."

If Redwood is flexible on the governing law point, Harper will accept narrowing the emergency relief carveout to the three categories above and include a short escalation/meet-and-confer requirement before filing. Alternatively, if Redwood stands firm on Delaware law, we would need stronger assurances (e.g., tolling and a defined short process to move provisional relief to Harper’s local jurisdiction for the limited categories).

Can Kimberly or your GC weigh in on the governing law trade-off — we’re trying to avoid a legal impasse that delays procurement.

Thanks — I’ve copied our outside counsel Maya Chen who annotated specific clauses.

— Ian
Ian Burke
Director, Procurement (Harper Health)

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — governing law, seat, and injunctive relief proposals

Ian / Harper team —

Thanks for the clear counter and the annotated redline. I’m Kimberly Park (Legal Ops / lead counsel on this account) — copying internal stakeholders so we’re aligned on the negotiation path. We discussed options with our GC and have a pragmatic compromise that should satisfy both sides and keep procurement moving.

Proposed compromise (legal):
1) Governing law: Delaware (commercial contract). Rationale: consistency with our enterprise contracts and predictability for interpretation.
2) Emergency relief carveout: explicit, narrowly tailored carveout permitting either party to seek provisional or injunctive relief in local courts (including Northern District of California) solely for: (a) preservation of evidence; (b) protection of trade secrets/IP; and (c) urgent data security incidents. The language will: (i) state the limited categories, (ii) require an expedited 48-hour meet-and-confer prior to filing where feasible, and (iii) include a clause stating such court filings do not waive the parties' agreement to arbitrate the merits.
3) Arbitration seat: San Francisco (if Harper insists on California-based seat) — Redwood can accept SF as the seat for arbitration hearings; however, the governing law will remain Delaware. That split (Delaware law + SF seat) is common and enforceable.

If Harper agrees to the limited scope of the injunctive carveout and the meet-and-confer, Redwood will: (a) accept SF as arbitration seat, (b) keep governing law as Delaware, and (c) update the MSA redline to include tolling language and an explicit statement that emergency court actions are limited in scope.

Please confirm by end of day Thursday (8/6) so we can prepare the clean MSA and send a DocuSign envelope. If Harper remains opposed to Delaware law entirely, we propose a short call between legal teams (Kimberly + Harper GC + Maya) to resolve quickly.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133

Thanks — that compromise works for Harper. We are willing to accept: Delaware governing law together with an explicit, narrowly tailored emergency relief carveout limited to preservation, trade secrets/IP, and urgent data/security issues, plus a 48-hour meet-and-confer. We also accept San Francisco as the arbitration seat.

Next steps: can you (1) incorporate the agreed language into a clean MSA, (2) send the updated document back to us for one last technical pass, and (3) open a DocuSign envelope for signature? Once we have the signed MSA Harper’s procurement team will issue the PO and contract countersign.

I’m copying Finance/Contracts so they see the ask. We appreciate the flexibility.
